lines.text: Lesson eleven: spot versus futures. What do you really own when you trade?
lines.say: Lesson eleven: spot versus futures. What do you really own when you trade?

lines.text: Asha and Rahul both think BTC might rise. Both trade 0.010 BTC at 60,000.
lines.say: Asha and Rahul both think B-T-C might rise. Both trade zero point zero one B-T-C at sixty thousand.

lines.text: Asha buys on spot. Rahul opens a long futures position.
lines.say: Asha buys on spot. Rahul opens a long futures position.

lines.text: If BTC rises, both gain. So what's the difference?
lines.say: If B-T-C rises, both gain. So what's the difference?

lines.text: Spot means buying the actual asset, paid in full, and it's yours right away.
lines.say: Spot means buying the actual asset, paid in full, and it's yours right away.

lines.text: Like buying a gold coin at a shop. You pay, and you take the coin home.
lines.say: Like buying a gold coin at a shop. You pay, and you take the coin home.

lines.text: Asha pays 600 USDT, and 0.010 BTC lands in her wallet. She owns it.
lines.say: Asha pays six hundred U-S-D-T, and zero point zero one B-T-C lands in her wallet. She owns it.

lines.text: A futures contract is an agreement about the price of an asset. It is not the asset itself.
lines.say: A futures contract is an agreement about the price of an asset. It is not the asset itself.

lines.text: The asset it follows is called the underlying. Here, the underlying is BTC.
lines.say: The asset it follows is called the underlying. Here, the underlying is B-T-C.

lines.text: Rahul opens a long contract for 0.010 BTC. No BTC arrives. He holds a contract.
lines.say: Rahul opens a long contract for zero point zero one B-T-C. No B-T-C arrives. He holds a contract.

lines.text: Most crypto futures are perpetual. A perpetual contract has no end date.
lines.say: Most crypto futures are perpetual. A perpetual contract has no end date.

lines.text: Older-style futures expire on a set date. A perpetual stays open until it's closed.
lines.say: Older-style futures expire on a set date. A perpetual stays open until it's closed.

lines.text: When it closes, profit or loss is settled in USDT. No coins are delivered.
lines.say: When it closes, profit or loss is settled in U-S-D-T. No coins are delivered.

lines.text: Exposure is how much of your money moves with the price.
lines.say: Exposure is how much of your money moves with the price.

lines.text: Notional value is the full size of a position: size × price.
lines.say: Notional value is the full size of a position: size times price.

lines.text: 0.010 BTC × 60,000 = 600 USDT. Asha and Rahul both have 600 USDT of exposure.
lines.say: Zero point zero one B-T-C times sixty thousand equals six hundred U-S-D-T. Asha and Rahul both have six hundred U-S-D-T of exposure.

lines.text: Now let's follow the same price for both, side by side.
lines.say: Now let's follow the same price for both, side by side.

lines.text: BTC rises to 63,000. Asha's coins are worth 630 USDT. Rahul's PnL is +30 USDT.
lines.say: B-T-C rises to sixty-three thousand. Asha's coins are worth six hundred thirty U-S-D-T. Rahul's P and L is plus thirty U-S-D-T.

lines.text: BTC falls to 57,000. Asha's coins: 570 USDT. Rahul's PnL: −30 USDT.
lines.say: B-T-C falls to fifty-seven thousand. Asha's coins: five hundred seventy U-S-D-T. Rahul's P and L: minus thirty U-S-D-T.

lines.text: Same moves, same money. But only Asha owns any BTC.
lines.say: Same moves, same money. But only Asha owns any B-T-C.

lines.text: Futures can also go short: you gain if the price falls, and lose if it rises.
lines.say: Futures can also go short: you gain if the price falls, and lose if it rises.

lines.text: Short 0.010 BTC from 60,000. At 57,000: +30 USDT. At 63,000: −30 USDT.
lines.say: Short zero point zero one B-T-C from sixty thousand. At fifty-seven thousand: plus thirty U-S-D-T. At sixty-three thousand: minus thirty U-S-D-T.

lines.text: On plain spot, you can only sell coins you already hold.
lines.say: On plain spot, you can only sell coins you already hold.

lines.text: A common mistake: thinking a futures position means you own the coin.
lines.say: A common mistake: thinking a futures position means you own the coin.

lines.text: You can't withdraw BTC from a futures position. There is no coin to send.
lines.say: You can't withdraw B-T-C from a futures position. There is no coin to send.

lines.text: Correction: futures give price exposure. Spot gives ownership.
lines.say: Correction: futures give price exposure. Spot gives ownership.

lines.text: Futures add risks that plain spot doesn't have.
lines.say: Futures add risks that plain spot doesn't have.

lines.text: Margin and leverage: a small deposit controls a bigger position. That's lesson T12.
lines.say: Margin and leverage: a small deposit controls a bigger position. That's lesson T twelve.

lines.text: Liquidation: if losses eat your margin, the exchange can close the position for you.
lines.say: Liquidation: if losses eat your margin, the exchange can close the position for you.

lines.text: Funding: perpetual traders pay or receive small amounts at set times. More in T13.
lines.say: Funding: perpetual traders pay or receive small amounts at set times. More in T thirteen.

lines.text: Your turn. Spot or futures? Sort these five. Pause if you need more time.
lines.say: Your turn. Spot or futures? Sort these five. Pause if you need more time.

lines.text: Holding coins in your wallet, and withdrawing them: spot.
lines.say: Holding coins in your wallet, and withdrawing them: spot.

lines.text: A perpetual long, funding payments and liquidation: all futures.
lines.say: A perpetual long, funding payments and liquidation: all futures.

lines.text: Well done if you sorted them all!
lines.say: Well done if you sorted them all!

lines.text: Here's the whole picture in one table.
lines.say: Here's the whole picture in one table.

lines.text: With spot, you hold the coin and pay the full price. No expiry, no funding, no liquidation.
lines.say: With spot, you hold the coin and pay the full price. No expiry, no funding, no liquidation.

lines.text: With perpetual futures, you hold a contract. You can go long or short.
lines.say: With perpetual futures, you hold a contract. You can go long or short.

lines.text: And you face funding and liquidation.
lines.say: And you face funding and liquidation.

lines.text: Neither one is safe. Spot prices can fall a lot, and you can lose money.
lines.say: Neither one is safe. Spot prices can fall a lot, and you can lose money.

lines.text: Futures can lose faster, and a position can be closed for you.
lines.say: Futures can lose faster, and a position can be closed for you.

lines.text: Fees and funding keep adding up while a futures position stays open.
lines.say: Fees and funding keep adding up while a futures position stays open.

lines.text: When unsure, WAIT. NO_TRADE is always allowed.
lines.say: When unsure, wait. No trade is always allowed.

lines.text: Spot means you buy and own the actual coin.
lines.say: Spot means you buy and own the actual coin.

lines.text: Futures are contracts about a price. You can go long or short, but you own no coin.
lines.say: Futures are contracts about a price. You can go long or short, but you own no coin.

lines.text: Futures add funding, leverage and liquidation risk.
lines.say: Futures add funding, leverage and liquidation risk.

lines.text: Check yourself: you hold a BTC perpetual long. Do you own any BTC?
lines.say: Check yourself: you hold a B-T-C perpetual long. Do you own any B-T-C?

lines.text: No. You hold a contract that follows the BTC price.
lines.say: No. You hold a contract that follows the B-T-C price.

lines.text: Great work! Next up, T12: margin and leverage, and why they magnify losses as well as gains.
lines.say: Great work! Next up, T twelve: margin and leverage, and why they magnify losses as well as gains.
